block.txt: Subject to subsection (2), the Children’s Guardian may delegate to an officer of the Children’s Guardian the exercise of a function of the Children’s Guardian.
The Children’s Guardian may not delegate the exercise of—
a function to make a report under this Act, other than to an Assistant Children’s Guardian, or
a function conferred by clause 1(2) of Schedule 3, other than to an Assistant Children’s Guardian, or
the power of delegation under subsection (1).
An officer to whom the exercise of a function has been delegated under subsection (1) may subdelegate the exercise of the function to—
another officer of the Children’s Guardian, or
a person, or a member of a class of persons, prescribed by the regulations or approved by the Children’s Guardian.

heading.b: Referral of matters to police and other investigative agencies

block.txt: This section applies if information obtained by the Children’s Guardian in the course of exercising the Children’s Guardian’s functions is—
information relating to a possible criminal offence under an Act or other law, or
information relating to grounds for possible disciplinary action under an Act or other law.
The Children’s Guardian may refer the information to—
the Commissioner of Police, or
the Ombudsman, or
the Secretary, or
a NSW, interstate or Commonwealth investigative or disciplinary government agency the Children’s Guardian considers appropriate.
However, this section does not apply to information obtained in the course of exercising functions under section 40A of the Child Protection (Working with Children) Act 2012.
Nothing in this section limits or affects the operation of Chapter 16A of the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998.
This section applies to the following entities—
the Children’s Guardian,
an advisory committee,
a member of an advisory committee,
a person acting under the direction of the Children’s Guardian,
an Official Community Visitor.

A matter or thing done, or omitted to be done, by an entity in good faith for the purposes of executing this or any other Act, does not subject the entity personally to any action, liability, claim or demand.
See also section 181 for protection from liability for an officer of the Children’s Guardian.

heading.b: Report required before commencement of Part 4

block.txt: Before the commencement of Part 4 of this Act, the Children’s Guardian must give to the Committee on Children and Young People a report, and copies of policies and procedures to be adopted by the Children’s Guardian, in relation to the exercise of the Children’s Guardian’s functions under this Act or another Act.

The report must include information about how perceived or actual conflicts of interest associated with the exercise of the Children’s Guardian’s functions under this Act or another Act are to be minimised or removed.
In this section—
Committee on Children and Young People means the Parliamentary Joint Committee constituted under section 36(1) of the Advocate for Children and Young People Act 2014.
In this Division, a reference to a Presiding Officer of a House of Parliament is a reference to the President of the Legislative Council or the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
If there is a vacancy in the office of President, the reference to the President is taken to be a reference to the Clerk of the Legislative Council.
If there is a vacancy in the office of Speaker, the reference to the Speaker is taken to be a reference to the Clerk of the Legislative Assembly.
The Children’s Guardian must—
prepare, within the period of 4 months after 30 June in each year, a report about the Children’s Guardian’s operations during the year ending on 30 June, and
give the report to the Presiding Officer of each House of Parliament.
A report by the Children’s Guardian under this section must include the following—
a description of the activities of the Children’s Guardian in relation to the functions of the Children’s Guardian,
details of each exemption given under section 30,

any recommendations for changes in the laws of the State, or for administrative action, the Children’s Guardian considers should be made as a result of the exercise of the functions of the Children’s Guardian,
an evaluation of the response of relevant entities to the recommendations of the Children’s Guardian,
a description of matters relating to reportable conduct, including trends, investigations and reports,
a description of the work and activities of Official Community Visitors, including information about—
the number of referrals made by the Children’s Guardian under section 150, and
the outcome of an investigation by the Children’s Guardian arising from a report by an Official Community Visitor,

the number of investigations or determinations, in relation to reportable allegations or reportable convictions, that have not been completed by a relevant entity or the Children’s Guardian within 6 months after the commencement of the investigation or determination,

the number of persons on the residential care workers register kept under section 85(1)(b) who have a reportable conduct flag noted, if the investigation or determination has not been completed by a relevant entity or the Children’s Guardian within 6 months after the commencement of the investigation or determination,

copies of policies and procedures to be adopted by the Children’s Guardian, in relation to the exercise of the Children’s Guardian’s functions under this Act or another Act, and information about how perceived or actual conflicts of interest associated with the exercise of the functions are to be minimised or removed.
Despite subsection (2), the report on the work and activities of Official Community Visitors may be a separate annual report.

heading.b: Special reports to Parliament and to Minister

block.txt: The Children’s Guardian may—
prepare a special report on a matter relating to the functions of the Children’s Guardian, and
give the report to the Presiding Officer of each House of Parliament.
Also, the Children’s Guardian, if requested by the Minister—
must prepare a special report on a matter relating to a function of the Children’s Guardian, other than a function under Part 4, and
may prepare a special report on a matter relating to a function of the Children’s Guardian under Part 4.

A special report prepared at the request of the Minister may be given by the Children’s Guardian to the Presiding Officer of each House of Parliament within 6 months after giving the report to the Minister.
The Children’s Guardian—
must give the Minister a draft of each of the reports to be given to the Presiding Officers under this Division, other than a special report mentioned in section 139(2)(b), and
may give the Minister a draft of a special report to be given to the Presiding Officers mentioned in section 139(2)(b).

A draft report that is required to be given to the Minister under subsection (1) must be given to the Minister at least one month, or a shorter period agreed by the Minister, before the report is given to the Presiding Officers.
The Minister may—
give the Children’s Guardian comments about a draft report, and
require the Children’s Guardian to consult further in relation to the report.

The Children’s Guardian is not required to amend the report because of comments made by the Minister but must, before finalising the report and giving it to the Presiding Officers, consider the comments.

heading.b: Provisions relating to reports to Parliament

block.txt: A copy of a report, given to the Presiding Officer of a House of Parliament under this Division, is to be laid before the House within 15 sitting days of the House after it is received by the Presiding Officer.
The Children’s Guardian may include a recommendation that the report be made public.

If a report includes a recommendation by the Children’s Guardian that the report be made public, the Presiding Officer of a House of Parliament given the report under this Division must, within 14 days after receiving the report, make it public whether or not the House is in session and whether or not the report has been laid before the House.
If a report is made public by a Presiding Officer of a House of Parliament before it is laid before the House, it attracts the same privileges and immunities as if it had been laid before the House.
A Presiding Officer need not inquire whether all or any conditions precedent have been satisfied in relation to a report given to the Presiding Officer under this Division.
The Government Sector Finance Act 2018 is, in its application to annual reporting information prepared for the Children’s Guardian, modified to the extent necessary for the purposes of this Part.
The objects of this Part are—
to protect and promote the rights of children in visitable services, and
to protect children from abuse, neglect and exploitation.
In this Part—
child in care means a child under the age of 18 years—
under the parental responsibility of the Minister administering the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998, or
for whom the Secretary or a designated agency has responsibility due to the operation of section 49 of the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998, or
who is a protected person under section 135A(3) of the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998, or
who is the subject of an out-of-home care arrangement under this Act or under the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998, or
who is the subject of an arrangement for specialised substitute residential care, or

who is the subject of a sole parental responsibility order made under section 149 of the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998, as in force immediately before its repeal by the Child Protection Legislation Amendment Act 2014, or
who is otherwise in the care of a service provider.
service includes a statutory or other function, and providing a service includes exercising such a function.
service provider means—
the Department, or
an implementation company under the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NSW Enabling) Act 2013 while the company is a public sector agency of the State under that Act, or
the Minister, or
an authorised carer or designated agency, or
a person or organisation funded, authorised or licensed by the Children’s Guardian or the Minister to provide a service, or
a person or organisation prescribed by the regulations.
visitable service means—
a service prescribed by the regulations as a visitable service.
The Minister may, on the recommendation of the Children’s Guardian, appoint a person as an Official Community Visitor if the person, in the opinion of the Minister—
has appropriate knowledge and expertise in the matters relating to children in care, and
has a commitment to the objects of this Act and the following Acts—
the Adoption Act 2000,
the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998,
the Children (Education and Care Services) Supplementary Provisions Act 2011,
the Disability Inclusion Act 2014,
the Community Welfare Act 1987,
the Community Services (Complaints, Reviews and Monitoring) Act 1993,
the Guardianship Act 1987, and
has skills in the solving of problems about access to, and the use of, services for children in care, and
is not employed within the Department or the Office of the Children’s Guardian.
An Official Community Visitor holds office for the term, not exceeding 3 years, stated in the instrument of appointment, and is eligible for re-appointment.
A person may not be appointed as an Official Community Visitor for consecutive terms totalling more than 6 years.
The provisions of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 relating to the employment of Public Service employees do not apply to an Official Community Visitor.

An Official Community Visitor is not a separate public sector agency and is to be regarded as part of the Department for the purposes of the Privacy and Personal Information Protection Act 1998 and the Health Records and Information Privacy Act 2002.
The Minister may, on the recommendation of the Children’s Guardian, remove an Official Community Visitor from office for incompetence, incapacity or misbehaviour.

To remove any doubt, an Official Community Visitor who has a disability (other than mental incapacity) may not be removed from office under subsection (6) on the ground of incapacity unless the disability renders the Official Community Visitor incapable of performing the functions of an Official Community Visitor.
An Official Community Visitor may—
enter and inspect a place where a visitable service is provided at a reasonable time, and
confer alone with a child who is resident or person employed at the visitable service, and

inspect a document held at a visitable service, if the document relates to the operation of a visitable service, having regard to the wishes of a child resident at the visitable service to whom the document relates, and
provide the Minister and the Children’s Guardian with advice or reports on any matters relating to the conduct of a visitable service, and
inform the Minister and the Children’s Guardian on matters affecting the welfare, interests and conditions of children using visitable services, and

encourage the promotion of legal and human rights of children using visitable services, including the right to privacy, confidentiality, adequate information and consultation in relation to visitable services and the right to complain, and
provide information about the Child Safe Standards to assist both the visitable services and the children using the services, and
provide the Secretary with information, advice or reports on the following matters—
matters relating to the conduct of places where visitable services are provided,
matters affecting the welfare, interests and conditions of children in visitable services, and

consider matters raised by children using visitable services, staff of providers of visitable services and people having a genuine concern for the welfare, interests and conditions of children using visitable services, and
provide information about independent advocacy services to help children in the presentation of a grievance or matter of concern and, in appropriate cases, assist children to obtain the services, and

facilitate, if reasonable and practicable, the early and speedy resolution of grievances or matters of concern affecting children using visitable services by referring grievances or matters to the providers of the relevant services or other appropriate bodies, and
exercise functions prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this section.

An Official Community Visitor must, in exercising a function under this section, act in a manner that preserves, as far as possible, the privacy of each child resident at the premises at which a visitable service is provided.

The Children’s Guardian has a general oversight and co-ordination role in relation to Official Community Visitors and may determine priorities for the services to be provided by Official Community Visitors.
The Children’s Guardian may convene meetings of Official Community Visitors, and take other action, as may be necessary for the exercise of the Children’s Guardian’s functions.
At least one meeting is to be held each calendar year.

heading.b: Report may be made to Children’s Guardian

block.txt: An Official Community Visitor may make a report to the Children’s Guardian about a child in care if the Official Community Visitor reasonably suspects the child’s safety, welfare or wellbeing is at risk.
The report does not need to be in writing.

The Children’s Guardian may make preliminary inquiries for the purposes of deciding how to deal with a report and may request further information from the Official Community Visitor making the report.
The Children’s Guardian may, in respect of a report—
conduct an investigation, or
make a referral to an entity, or
decline to take action on the report.

If an Official Community Visitor, acting in good faith, makes a report to the Children’s Guardian under this section, the person is not liable to civil or criminal action, or disciplinary action, for making the report.

The Children’s Guardian may, at the Children’s Guardian’s own initiative, decide to deal with a matter as a report under this section if the matter relates to a child in care that the Children’s Guardian reasonably suspects is not safe, or if the Children’s Guardian has concerns for the welfare or wellbeing of the child.
Schedule 2 provides for powers that may be exercised by the Children’s Guardian or an authorised person under this Act in relation to an investigation under this Part.

heading.b: Powers of Children’s Guardian to conduct inquiry

block.txt: For the purposes of an investigation of a report under section 147, the Children’s Guardian may conduct an inquiry.
Schedule 3 provides for powers that may be exercised by the Children’s Guardian for the inquiry.

This section applies if the Children’s Guardian is of the opinion that a report, or part of a report, given under section 147 constitutes a report, complaint or other matter that may be made to one or more of the following entities—
the Commissioner of the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission under the National Disability Insurance Scheme Act 2013 of the Commonwealth,
the Ageing and Disability Commissioner under the Ageing and Disability Commissioner Act 2019,
the Secretary,
the Ombudsman,
an entity prescribed by the regulations.
The Children’s Guardian must refer the report, or the part of the report, to the entity.
The Children’s Guardian must determine, with the entity the report is referred to, the most appropriate entity to conduct the investigation of the report.

Despite subsection (3), if the Children’s Guardian is of the opinion that conducting an investigation may be necessary to protect the safety, welfare or wellbeing of a child, or class of children, the Children’s Guardian may conduct an investigation of the report referred to the entity, including in consultation with the entity.

heading.b: Provision of information to Children’s Guardian

block.txt: This section applies to information of a class that the Children’s Guardian has determined is information relevant to the exercise of the functions of the Children’s Guardian in connection with—
the accreditation of designated agencies, or
specialised substitute residential care.

An Official Community Visitor is required to provide to the Children’s Guardian, and the Children’s Guardian is authorised to collect and use, information belonging to a class referred to in subsection (1), if the Children’s Guardian has notified the Official Community Visitor the information belongs to the class.

A provision of an Act or law that prohibits or restricts the disclosure of information does not operate to prevent the provision of information, or affect a duty to provide information, under this section.
A person must not take or threaten to take detrimental action—
against an Official Community Visitor, or
in respect of a person because that person, in good faith, makes, or proposes to make, a complaint under this Part.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units or imprisonment for 12 months, or both.
For subsection (1)(b), a complaint is not made in good faith if—
the report, complaint or notification was made or proposed in bad faith, or
a material allegation was known, by the person giving the report, complaint or notification, to be false.
In this section—
community service has the same meaning as in the Community Services (Complaints, Reviews and Monitoring) Act 1993.
complaint includes providing information, documents or evidence in relation to a complaint under this Part.
detrimental action means action causing, comprising or involving any of the following—
injury, damage or loss,
intimidation or harassment,
discrimination, disadvantage or adverse treatment in relation to employment,
dismissal from, or prejudice in, employment,
prejudice in the provision of a community service,
disciplinary proceedings.

If the Children’s Guardian reasonably believes a child safe organisation’s systems, policies or processes do not reflect or implement the Child Safe Standards, the Children’s Guardian may issue a compliance notice requiring the organisation to—
take the action specified in the notice, and
provide the Children’s Guardian with evidence it has done so.
A compliance notice must be in writing and must include—
the reasons for the belief the relevant child safe organisation’s systems, policies or processes do not reflect or implement the Child Safe Standards, and
the risks to children that arise because the organisation’s systems, policies or processes do not reflect or implement the Child Safe Standards, and
the action the organisation is required to take, and
the period of time within which the organisation is required to take the action, and
a statement that failure to comply with a compliance notice is an offence.
The period of time for the organisation to take the action required by the compliance notice must be reasonable in all the circumstances.
A child safe organisation that is issued a compliance notice may, within 28 days of receiving the notice, request the Children’s Guardian to review the decision to issue the notice.
The Children’s Guardian must comply with a request made under subsection (1) unless, in the opinion of the Children’s Guardian, the request is frivolous or vexatious.
An organisation that requests a review may provide the Children’s Guardian with the information the organisation considers relevant to the review.
An organisation that requests a review is not required to comply with the notice while the review is underway.
Following a review, the Children’s Guardian may—
confirm the decision to issue the compliance notice, or
withdraw the compliance notice.

If the review confirms the decision to issue the compliance notice, the Children’s Guardian must give the organisation a reasonable time to comply with the notice, being a period of not less than 28 days after the compliance notice is given to the organisation.
If, following the review, the Children’s Guardian withdraws the notice, the notice may be reissued—
in substantially the same form, or
in a different form.

heading.b: Extension of time for compliance with compliance notices

block.txt: A child safe organisation that has been issued with a compliance notice may apply to the Children’s Guardian for an extension of time for compliance.
The organisation may only apply for an extension of time if the application is made before the end of the period of time it is applying to extend.
The Children’s Guardian may grant an application made under this section if the Children’s Guardian considers—
the organisation has taken suitable steps to address the risks to children identified in the notice, and
there are special circumstances justifying the extension of time.

heading.b: Compliance notices to be publicly available

block.txt: The Children’s Guardian is to maintain a list of compliance notices that are in effect and make the list publicly available on the Office of the Children’s Guardian’s website.
A child safe organisation that produces an annual report must include in the report the details of a compliance notice that applied to the organisation during the period covered by the report.
This section does not apply to a compliance notice until—
the expiry of the 28 day period in which the organisation may apply for a review of the decision to issue the notice, or
the conclusion of a review under section 152C.
A child safe organisation that receives a compliance notice must comply with the notice.
Maximum penalty—
for a corporation—250 penalty units, or
otherwise—50 penalty units.
If a child safe organisation is not a person the reference in subsection (1) to a child safe organisation is to be read as a reference to the head of a child safe organisation.
Instead of issuing a compliance notice under Division 1, the Children’s Guardian may accept an enforceable undertaking from a child safe organisation.
An enforceable undertaking is an undertaking from the organisation under which the organisation agrees to take specific action by a specific date.
An enforceable undertaking must be in writing and be signed by the head of the organisation.
This section applies if a child safe organisation has entered into an enforceable undertaking.
The organisation may apply to the Children’s Guardian to amend the undertaking.
The organisation may only apply to amend an undertaking if the application is made before the date by which the organisation had agreed to undertake the action specified in the undertaking.
The Children’s Guardian may only agree to amendment of an undertaking if the Children’s Guardian considers—
the organisation has taken suitable steps to address the risks to children that led to the undertaking, and
amendment of the undertaking is appropriate in all the circumstances.

heading.b: Enforceable undertakings to be publicly available

block.txt: The Children’s Guardian is to maintain a list of enforceable undertakings that are in effect and make the list publicly available on the Office of the Children’s Guardian’s website.
A child safe organisation that produces an annual report must include in the report the details of an enforceable undertaking that applied to the organisation during the period covered by the report.
A child safe organisation that enters into an enforceable undertaking must comply with the undertaking.
Maximum penalty—
for a corporation—500 penalty units, or
otherwise—100 penalty units.
If a child safe organisation is not a person the reference in subsection (1) to a child safe organisation is to be read as a reference to the head of a child safe organisation.

The Children’s Guardian must inform the Minister when taking enforcement action under this Part against a child safe organisation that is a public authority under section 14, definition of public authority, paragraphs (a), (b), (d) or (e).
In this Part—
service provider has the same meaning as in section 143, and also means a relevant entity under Part 4.

heading.b: Applications to Civil and Administrative Tribunal for administrative review

block.txt: An application may be made to the Civil and Administrative Tribunal under the Administrative Decisions Review Act 1997 for administrative review of the following decisions—
a decision of the Children’s Guardian to do or refuse to do the following in relation to accreditation as a designated agency or an accredited adoption service provider—
grant accreditation,
impose a condition on an accreditation or vary the conditions to which an accreditation is subject,
transfer an accreditation,
cancel or shorten the period of an accreditation,
a decision of the Children’s Guardian—
to grant an employer’s authority, or
to impose a condition or further conditions on, or to vary or revoke a condition of, an employer’s authority, or
to suspend or revoke an employer’s authority,
a decision of the Children’s Guardian to declare under section 91(b) that a person is taken to be the employer of a child,
a decision of the Children’s Guardian to grant an exemption under section 102, to revoke the exemption or to impose conditions on the exemption,

The Children’s Guardian may, at any time, by written notice to an accreditation holder, vary the conditions of the accreditation imposed by the Children’s Guardian.
A variation includes the following—
the imposition of a new condition,
the substitution of a condition,
the removal of a condition,
the amendment of a condition.

heading.b: Condition limiting adoption services that may be provided

block.txt: The Children’s Guardian may impose a condition on an accreditation limiting the adoption services that may be provided under the accreditation.

heading.b: Condition requiring compliance with accreditation criteria

block.txt: The Children’s Guardian must impose a condition on accreditation requiring the holder of the accreditation to wholly meet the accreditation criteria within 12 months if—
the Children’s Guardian grants accreditation to the holder, and
the Children’s Guardian is of the opinion the holder substantially meets the accreditation criteria but does not wholly meet the criteria.

It is a condition of a provisional accreditation that the holder of the accreditation give written notice to the Children’s Guardian as soon as practicable after the holder first provides adoption services under the accreditation.
The Children’s Guardian may transfer the accreditation of an organisation (the former organisation) to another organisation (the new organisation) if satisfied that—

because of a restructure involving the former organisation, the new organisation will be exercising the accredited adoption service provider functions previously exercised by the former organisation, or
the former organisation has been merged with, or acquired by, the new organisation, or
the accreditation should be transferred because of circumstances prescribed by the regulations.
The holder of an accreditation may surrender the accreditation.
The Children’s Guardian may require the surrender not to occur until a date decided by the Children’s Guardian not more than 6 months after the holder applies to surrender the accreditation.
In deciding on a date, the Children’s Guardian must consider the safety, welfare and wellbeing of children who may be affected by the decision.
A failure by the holder to apply to renew accreditation is taken to be an application to surrender an accreditation except as provided by the regulations.
An accreditation remains in force until the date decided by the Children’s Guardian under subclause (2).

heading.b: Cancelling or shortening period of accreditation
Grounds for cancelling or shortening period of accreditation

block.txt: Each of the following constitutes grounds for cancelling or shortening the period of an accreditation—
the holder of the accreditation is not suitable to be accredited,
the accreditation was granted in error,
a ground prescribed by the regulations.

heading.b: How accreditation is cancelled or shortened

block.txt: The Children’s Guardian may, by written notice given to the holder of an accreditation, cancel or shorten the period of the accreditation if the Children’s Guardian is satisfied there are grounds for the cancellation or shortening.
A notice cancelling an accreditation must specify—
the date or time from which cancellation takes effect, and
the grounds for the cancellation.
A notice shortening the period of an accreditation must specify—
the date on which the shortened accreditation will cease to have effect, and
the grounds for the shortening of the period of accreditation.

The Children’s Guardian may, by further written notice given to the holder of an accreditation while the accreditation is in force, amend or revoke a notice cancelling or shortening the period of the accreditation.
If an accreditation is cancelled, the holder of the accreditation is disqualified from being accredited for 2 years after the cancellation takes effect.
Regulations may be made about accreditation, including the following—
applications for accreditation,
the withdrawal of applications,
the deferral of decisions and the obligations the Children’s Guardian may impose on an applicant during the period of the deferral,
conditions of accreditation and applications for variation of conditions of accreditation,
transfers of accreditation,
surrenders of accreditation.
The regulations may contain provisions of a savings or transitional nature consequent on the commencement of—
a provision of this Act, or
a provision amending this Act.
A savings or transitional provision consequent on the commencement of a provision must not be made more than 2 years after the commencement.
A savings or transitional provision made consequent on the commencement of a provision is repealed 2 years after the commencement.
A savings or transitional provision made consequent on the commencement of a provision may take effect before the commencement but not before—
for a provision of this Act—the date of assent to this Act, or
for a provision amending this Act—the date of assent to the amending Act.
A savings or transitional provision taking effect before its publication on the NSW legislation website does not—
affect the rights of a person existing before the publication in a way prejudicial to the person, or
impose liabilities on a person for anything done or omitted to be done before the publication.
In this clause—
person does not include the State or an authority of the State.
This clause applies to regulations made under the following Acts—
the Adoption Act 2000,
the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998,
the Community Services (Complaints, Reviews and Monitoring) Act 1993,
the Ombudsman Act 1974.

A provision of a regulation made under an Act listed in subclause (1) continues in force despite the commencement of this Act or a regulation under this Act, as if the provision of the regulation were made under a provision of this Act, with the necessary modifications.
This clause expires on 1 September 2022.

heading.b: Provisions consequent on enactment of this Act

block.txt: The appointment of the Children’s Guardian under the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998 is continued as if the appointment were made under this Act.

heading.b: Existing accreditation and applications for accreditation

block.txt: An organisation that, immediately before the commencement, was accredited as an adoption service provider under Part 2 of Chapter 3 of the Adoption Act 2000 is taken to have been accredited under this Act for the period and subject to the conditions to which it was subject.

An application for accreditation made by an organisation under Part 2 of Chapter 3 of the Adoption Act 2000 before the commencement of this Act, and not finally dealt with, is to continue to be dealt with under that Part unless the applicant elects to have the application dealt with under this Act.

heading.b: Criteria for accreditation under Adoption Act 2000

block.txt: The standards and other criteria, approved under section 13 of the Adoption Act 2000, are taken to be standards and other criteria under section 113 of this Act.
Section 75 of this Act extends to things done by, or with the approval of, a principal officer under section 5A of the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998.

A person who, immediately before the commencement, was an Official Community Visitor for the purposes of Part 2 of the Community Services (Complaints, Reviews and Monitoring) Act 1993, is taken to have been appointed as an Official Community Visitor under section 144 of this Act for the term for which the person was appointed under section 7 of the Community Services (Complaints, Reviews and Monitoring) Act 1993.
Nothing in this clause limits any function an Official Community Visitor may have under any other Act.

This clause applies to the following entities registered or otherwise authorised to arrange or provide voluntary out-of-home care in accordance with the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998 (each a voluntary out-of-home care agency)—
a designated agency,
a registered agency,
an individual authorised by a relevant agency (within the meaning of section 156 of that Act) or the Children’s Guardian to provide voluntary out-of-home care.

A voluntary out-of-home care agency, registered under the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998 and the regulations under that Act to arrange or provide voluntary out-of-home care, is, on commencement, taken to be—
the equivalent type of voluntary out-of-home care agency under this Act, and
registered under this Act for the period and subject to the conditions to which it was subject under the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998.

An application for registration as a voluntary out-of-home care agency made under the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998 and the regulations under that Act is, on commencement, taken to be an application for registration as the equivalent type of voluntary out-of-home care agency registration and is to be determined in accordance with this Act.
Records kept in relation to Part 3A of the Ombudsman Act 1974 are to be transferred to the Office of the Children’s Guardian on commencement.

A transferred record is to be treated for the purposes of a law of the State as if it were a record that the Children’s Guardian had lawfully obtained in the performance of the Children’s Guardian’s functions.

However, the provisions of the Ombudsman Act 1974, as in force immediately before the commencement of this Schedule, continue to apply to records transferred by operation of this clause, as if they had not been transferred.
This clause has effect despite section 21 of the State Records Act 1998 and section 34 of the Ombudsman Act 1974.
Nothing in this Act prevents the Ombudsman from accessing records transferred under this clause, in the way agreed to by the Children’s Guardian.

heading.b: Reportable allegations and reportable convictions under the Ombudsman Act 1974

block.txt: On commencement, an existing matter is taken to be a reportable allegation or reportable conviction made to the Children’s Guardian under this Act.
In this clause—

existing matter means an investigation, notification or disclosure in relation to a reportable allegation or reportable conviction under Part 3A of the Ombudsman Act 1974 that is not finally dealt with on commencement.

If an entity commits an offence against a provision of Part 4 of this Act, other than an offence under Division 13 or Part 11 of this Act, the entity is taken not to have committed the offence for the period starting on commencement and ending 3 months after commencement.

heading.b: Annual reports not required in first 12 months of commencement

block.txt: Division 6 of Part 8 of this Act does not apply, in relation to an annual report, until 12 months after commencement of this Act.

heading.b: Provisions consequent on enactment of Children’s Guardian Amendment Act 2022

block.txt: In this Part—
amending Act means the Children’s Guardian Amendment Act 2022.
commencement day means 1 September 2022.
existing accreditation means accreditation, in force immediately before the commencement day, as—
a designated agency under the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Regulation 2012, or
an adoption service provider under this Act.

An amendment made to this Act by the amending Act does not affect an existing accreditation and the accreditation continues in force in the same form and for the same period as if the amending Act had not commenced.
Despite subclause (1)—
Schedule 3A, including relevant provisions, applies to an existing accreditation of a designated agency as if the accreditation had been granted under that Schedule, and
Schedule 3B, including relevant provisions, applies to an existing accreditation of an adoption service provider as if the accreditation had been granted under that Schedule.
In this clause—
relevant provisions means provisions enabling the Children’s Guardian to vary the conditions of accreditation or cancel or shorten the period of accreditation.

The standards and criteria approved by the Minister under the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Regulation 2012, clause 48 are taken to be the accreditation criteria for designated agencies approved by the Minister under Schedule 3A, clause 2.
Subclause (1) ceases to apply when the Minister approves accreditation criteria for designated agencies under Schedule 3A, clause 2.

The standards and criteria approved by the Minister under this Act, section 113 are taken to be the accreditation criteria for accredited adoption service providers approved by the Minister under Schedule 3B, clause 2.
Subclause (3) ceases to apply when the Minister approves accreditation criteria for accredited adoption service providers under Schedule 3B, clause 2.

heading.b: Accreditation criteria must be wholly satisfied

block.txt: The Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Regulation 2012, clause 54 as in force immediately before the commencement day continues to apply to an existing accreditation of a designated agency as if that clause were a provision of this Act.

An application for accreditation as a designated agency or an adoption service provider made before the commencement day, including an application for which a decision is deferred, must be dealt with as if the amending Act had not commenced.
If the application is granted, it is taken to have been granted under this Act as amended by the amending Act.
An application to transfer the accreditation as a designated agency or an adoption service provider must be dealt with as if the amending Act had not commenced.
However, the application must be dealt with as if the amending Act had commenced if the applicant elects to have it dealt with in this way.

heading.b: Children in specialised substitute residential care

block.txt: Time spent in specialised substitute residential care before the commencement of section 8ZA is to be taken into account for the purposes of that section.
Section 85(1C)(b) does not extend to include a person who ceased to be a residential care worker before the commencement of that paragraph.

The specialised substitute residential care register in section 85(1)(c) (the new register) is taken to be a continuation of the register for organisations that provide or arrange voluntary out-of-home care (the former register) that was referred to in that paragraph before the commencement day.
Information on the former register may be kept on the new register.

Extension of amendment to age requirement for Children’s Guardian

block.txt: Section 121, as amended by the Justice Legislation Amendment (Miscellaneous) Act 2023, extends to the person who held office as Children’s Guardian immediately before the commencement of the amendment.
